decisions.reason: The one-hour due-diligence arrangement changes only the preliminary assessment method and outputs; it does not alter the required style system or its coverage across templates.
Testing templates during due diligence may examine copy-paste errors, but the source does not change the existing legacy copy-paste stability behavior, test sources, or target version.
Documenting template errors during the assessment does not resolve the existing table-adjustment ambiguity or change the required table and column layout behavior.
The source establishes an assessment budget, method, and reporting outputs without changing any bullet appearance criterion.
The due-diligence task may test list behavior, but it does not change the required Tab-key behavior or list-hierarchy alignment.
The assessment may identify line-break errors, but the source does not modify the requirement that manual line breaks work reliably after pasted content.
